newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SW DISTRICTS EAGLES SAVAGE BLUE BULLS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SW DISTRICTS EAGLES SAVAGE BLUE BULLS.

text.p: South Western Districts Eagles produced the upset of the Currie Cup season -- of any Currie Cup season -- by defeating Northern Transvaal in their Loftus Versfeld laager on Friday night.
The Eagles conceded more than 100 points in each of their final three Currie Cup matches last season but are a changed side this year.

Former Northern Transvaal B coach Phil Pretorius recruited aggressively from the strong Carlton League in Pretoria during the close season and his team of exiles came up trumps with a richly deserved 30-18 win on Friday.
Eight of the side he fielded against Northerns had turned out for the Blue Bulls and their greater hunger and commitment paid off.
They restricted the home side to six Casper Steyn penalties while scoring three tries themselves through centre Conrad Stoltz, flanker Anton Leonard and lock Botha Rossouw.
To put the result into context, the men from George lost by a record 147-8 to Northerns last season.
The sending off of Eastern Province lock Adri Geldenhuys with 20 minutes remaining was the turning point in a close fought match with Boland in Port Elizabeth on Sunday.
E.P. had overturned a 17-7 halftime deficit to lead 20-17 at that point but the loss of Geldenhuys for a punch signalled a Boland revival.
Full-back Marius Goosen and centre McNeil Hendricks each scored their second tries to give their team maximum points.

Breyton Paulse's recall to the Western Province starting line-up paid off handsomely as the Springbok tourist scored five of his side's 11 tries in a 75-32 victory over the Gauteng Falcons (formerly Eastern Transvaal).
Paulse, regarded as too small and frail, had fallen out of favour at Newlands but he grabbed his chance brilliantly against a pedestrian Falcons side.

The left wing scored three of his tries with elusive running from deep inside his own half as W.P's backs ran riot. Springbok squad member Percival Montgomery and right wing Pieter Rossouw each scored two.
The Falcons at least had the consolation of taking a point from the game having scored four tries of their own -- two of them from interceptions.
Border's disappointing season went from bad to worse as they conceded eight tries in a 66-15 defeat by Western Transvaal (soon to be renamed North West) in Potchefstroom.
Centre AJ de Jager scored a hat-trick and wing Charles Bensch claimed a brace as Border's tackling wilted under a furious home assualt.
Free State overcame a sluggish start to swamp Mpumalanga 56-19 in Witbank.
Springbok sevens player Stephen Brink scored a hat-trick from the wing. The home side held out until the second quarter before conceding the first of eight tries.
